CastleStealer/Starland RAT accessing browser credential stores and crypto wallets AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the UAT-11795 collection stage where CastleStealer/Starland RAT (running under python.exe or the injected chain) reads browser Login Data / cookie DBs and cryptocurrency wallet files (wallet.dat, keystore) plus Discord/Telegram/Steam session data. Detects non-browser processes touching these sensitive stores. Rationale: Corroborators confirm CastleStealer/Starland RAT targets browser Login Data, 40+ crypto wallets (wallet.dat/keystore/Exodus), and Discord/Telegram/Steam sessions; scoping the access to python/script-host processes (not the browsers themselves) makes credential-store reads high-signal. Cross-checked against: • https://gbhackers.com/starland-rat-steals-browser-credentials/ • https://securityaffairs.com/195532/malware/new-russian-campaign-uses-fake-webex-and-zoom-installers-to-deploy-starland-rat.html
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1555 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Browser backup/sync utilities written in Python reading Login Data
  • Password-manager import tools accessing logins.json
  • Legitimate wallet backup scripts touching wallet.dat
  • EDR/DLP agents enumerating these paths for inventory
  • A developer debugging a Chromium profile with a python script
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "backup" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has "\\Program Files\\"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm the accessing process is not a sanctioned backup/sync tool; capture its parent chain (installer → python → collection). Step 2 (contain): Isolate the host, force-reset credentials for browsers/accounts stored on it, and move any crypto wallet assets to a clean device. Step 3 (hunt): Look for exfil to campaign C2 domains, staged archives (zip/7z) in temp, and parallel Remcos RAT indicators on the same or peer hosts.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\User Data\", "Login Data", @"\Network\Cookies", "logins.json", "wallet.dat", @"\Ethereum\keystore\", @"\Exodus\", @"\discord\Local Storage\", @"\Telegram Desktop\tdata\")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","pythonw.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","mshta.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\User Data\", "Login Data", @"\Network\Cookies", "logins.json", "wallet.dat", @"\Ethereum\keystore\", @"\Exodus\", @"\discord\Local Storage\", @"\Telegram Desktop\tdata\")
| where tolower(ActingProcessName) has_any ("python.exe","pythonw.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","mshta.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "b8be9a5e0a191050f9099c11c155b436863e9bc43bc904cdb842e249679aa35a", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a", "0398df5a18f71efcfeef4571a2cef577") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "b8be9a5e0a191050f9099c11c155b436863e9bc43bc904cdb842e249679aa35a", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a", "0398df5a18f71efcfeef4571a2cef577") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "b8be9a5e0a191050f9099c11c155b436863e9bc43bc904cdb842e249679aa35a", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a", "0398df5a18f71efcfeef4571a2cef577")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "b8be9a5e0a191050f9099c11c155b436863e9bc43bc904cdb842e249679aa35a", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a", "0398df5a18f71efcfeef4571a2cef577") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "b8be9a5e0a191050f9099c11c155b436863e9bc43bc904cdb842e249679aa35a", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a", "0398df5a18f71efcfeef4571a2cef577") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "b8be9a5e0a191050f9099c11c155b436863e9bc43bc904cdb842e249679aa35a", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a", "0398df5a18f71efcfeef4571a2cef577")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "b8be9a5e0a191050f9099c11c155b436863e9bc43bc904cdb842e249679aa35a", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a", "0398df5a18f71efcfeef4571a2cef577"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] HelloInjector DLL side-load: wtsapi32.dll dropped into ViPNet Update System dir · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] HelloNet renamed-PuTTY reverse SSH tunnel to 5.39.253.206 · [LLM] HelloProxy C2-handler artifact: tesh4RPC.txt written to C:\Users\Public · [LLM] HelloNet C2 egress to 5.39.253.206 / 176.32.34.135 · [LLM] HelloProxy listener: svchost.exe binding TCP 5003/5060 · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
HelloInjector DLL side-load: wtsapi32.dll dropped into ViPNet Update System dir AIInstallation High
Hunts the HelloNet persistence primitive: a malicious wtsapi32.dll written into C:\Program Files (x86)\InfoTeCS\VIPNet Update System so the auto-start itcsrvup64.exe binary side-loads it. Legitimate wtsapi32.dll only ships in System32/SysWOW64, so any copy under the InfoTeCS tree is anomalous by definition. Rationale: Anchored on the exact file (wtsapi32.dll) and exact path (\InfoTeCS\VIPNet Update System\) named in the article; the genuine DLL never lives here so any hit is the side-load. Cross-checked against Securelist, BleepingComputer and secnews.gr. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/tr/hellonet-vipnet/120700/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/hackers-abuse-vipnet-software-to-target-russian-govt-agencies/ • https://www.secnews.gr/en/722370/vipnet-update-mechanism-attack/
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • InfoTeCS-signed ViPNet update that legitimately stages a wtsapi32.dll (verify signer + hash against known-good)
  • Security-tool file-integrity backup copying System32 DLLs into a vendor folder
  • Analyst/IR staging a sample copy of the DLL into that path during investigation
  • Third-party installer temporarily extracting to the InfoTeCS directory
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "msiexec.exe" and InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName has "InfoTeCS")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: pull SHA256 of the dropped wtsapi32.dll and compare to the article/VT IOCs; check digital signature — genuine InfoTeCS DLLs are signed, the implant is not. Note InitiatingProcess that wrote it. 2) CONTAIN: isolate the host, kill/suspend itcsrvup64.exe and any svchost -netsvcs it spawned, quarantine the DLL, block C2 5.39.253.206 and 176.32.34.135 at the egress. 3) HUNT: sweep all ViPNet hosts for the same file/hash, then pivot to UC5/UC6 (C2 egress, svchost listeners on 5003/5060) and UC2 (renamed-PuTTY tunnel) on affected assets.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "wtsapi32.dll"
| where FolderPath has @"\InfoTeCS\VIPNet Update System\"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "wtsapi32.dll"
| where TargetFilePath has @"\InfoTeCS\VIPNet Update System\"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

HelloNet renamed-PuTTY reverse SSH tunnel to 5.39.253.206 AICommand & Control High
Hunts the operator's egress tunnel: a renamed legitimate PuTTY binary (frontpage.exe) launched from C:\users\public\music with reverse-forward flags (-N -R 8443:...:5003) to sftp@5.39.253.206 on port 3522. Matches on either the C2 IP + reverse-tunnel flag or the specific masqueraded path. Rationale: Uses the article's verbatim tunnel command (frontpage.exe -N -R 8443:...:5003 sftp@5.39.253.206 -P 3522) — the C2 IP plus reverse-tunnel flag is a two-token high-fidelity pair, and the public\music\frontpage.exe masquerade path is a standalone IOC. Confirmed by SC Media and Securelist. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/tr/hellonet-vipnet/120700/ • https://www.scworld.com/brief/hellonet-campaign-abuses-vipnet-update-mechanism-to-target-russian-organizations
ATT&CKT1572 T1021.004 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate admin running plink/PuTTY with -R for authorized reverse port-forwarding (but not to 5.39.253.206)
  • A benign but oddly-named frontpage.exe in a non-public path (path clause scopes this out)
  • Developer SSH tunnels for testing that happen to use -R (IP clause scopes this out)
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath has @"\Program Files" and ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName has "PuTTY" and not (ProcessCommandLine has "5.39.253.206"))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: confirm the destination IP/port (5.39.253.206:3522) and decode the -R forward target/port; verify the binary hash is PuTTY despite the frontpage.exe name. 2) CONTAIN: kill the process, block 5.39.253.206 outbound, isolate the host, capture the -pw credential argument if present and force-rotate any exposed creds. 3) HUNT: search all hosts for frontpage.exe under public\music and for any process talking to 5.39.253.206/176.32.34.135; correlate to UC1 side-load host and UC6 svchost listeners.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where (ProcessCommandLine has "-R" and ProcessCommandLine has "5.39.253.206")
    or (FileName =~ "frontpage.exe" and FolderPath has @"\users\public\music\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where (TargetProcessCommandLine has "-R" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "5.39.253.206")
    or (TargetProcessName has @"\users\public\music\frontpage.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: HelloNet Renamed PuTTY Reverse SSH Tunnel to C2 5.39.253.206

HelloProxy C2-handler artifact: tesh4RPC.txt written to C:\Users\Public AICommand & Control High
Hunts the HelloProxy operational log file tesh4RPC.txt (dropped in C:\users\public), which the AFD_RECV hook writes for every incoming C2 message as 'threadid: <id> pid=<pid>'. The filename is a unique campaign artifact with no legitimate use. Rationale: tesh4RPC.txt is a unique, non-dictionary filename named verbatim in the article as the HelloProxy C2-message log — effectively a signature with near-zero benign collision. Article-only IOC but so specific it warrants shipping. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/tr/hellonet-vipnet/120700/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Effectively none — the filename is a bespoke campaign artifact
  • IR/analyst copying the sample or its output into a public path during triage
  • Backup/EDR quarantine writing a file with this name into a staging folder
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: read the file (threadid/pid lines confirm C2 activity) and identify the InitiatingProcess — expect svchost.exe (netsvcs). 2) CONTAIN: isolate the host, suspend the offending svchost, block 5.39.253.206/176.32.34.135, and preserve the file for evidence before quarantine. 3) HUNT: sweep all hosts for tesh4RPC.txt, then pivot to the side-load DLL (UC1), C2 egress (UC5) and svchost listeners on 5003/5060 (UC6) on any host that has it.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "tesh4RPC.txt"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "tesh4RPC.txt"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

HelloExecutor recon enumerating ViPNet Client/Administrator Export key stores AIReconnaissance Medium
Hunts the HelloExecutor reconnaissance step where the operator runs dir against ViPNet key-export directories (ViPNet Client\Export and ViPNet Administrator\kc\Export) to locate exportable network keys. These exact enumeration paths are the campaign's stated objective and are not part of normal admin activity. Rationale: Uses the article's exact recon target paths (ViPNet Client\Export, ViPNet Administrator\kc\Export) which hold exportable network keys — the stated attacker objective. Kept at hunting/medium because a ViPNet admin could legitimately list these dirs, but the path specificity keeps FPs low. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/tr/hellonet-vipnet/120700/ • https://www.secnews.gr/en/722370/vipnet-update-mechanism-attack/
ATT&CKT1083 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • ViPNet administrator legitimately browsing the Export folder during key distribution
  • Backup software enumerating the infotecs directory tree
  • Inventory/asset-management scripts recursing Program Files (x86)
  • Helpdesk troubleshooting a ViPNet Client key issue
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("explorer.exe","mmc.exe") and not (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "cmd.exe" and IsInitiatingProcessRemoteSession == false and InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "explorer.exe")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: identify the parent process — HelloExecutor runs via injected svchost.exe, whereas a real admin runs from explorer/cmd interactively; check for the sibling recon burst (query user, ipconfig /all, net group /do, ping 8.8.8.8 -n 1) on the same host/session. 2) CONTAIN: if parent is svchost/non-interactive, isolate the host and suspend the process; else confirm with the named admin. 3) HUNT: pivot to UC1 (side-load DLL), UC5/UC6 (C2) and check whether any Export key material was subsequently staged or exfiltrated via the UC2 tunnel.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ProcessCommandLine contains @"ViPNet Client\Export"
    or ProcessCommandLine contains @"ViPNet Administrator\kc\Export"
    or (ProcessCommandLine has "infotecs" and ProcessCommandLine has "Export")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetProcessCommandLine contains @"ViPNet Client\Export"
    or TargetProcessCommandLine contains @"ViPNet Administrator\kc\Export"
    or (TargetProcessCommandLine has "infotecs" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "Export")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

HelloNet C2 egress to 5.39.253.206 / 176.32.34.135 AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts any outbound connection to the two confirmed HelloNet command-and-control IPs (5.39.253.206 — also the SSH tunnel endpoint on 3522 — and 176.32.34.135). A flat IOC-match detection to catch beacon, tunnel, or proxy traffic regardless of the originating process. Rationale: Two hard network IOCs named in the article; 5.39.253.206 is doubly confirmed as both the SSH-tunnel endpoint (port 3522) and the proxy C2. Flat IOC match, alerting tier. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/tr/hellonet-vipnet/120700/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1572
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel scanner or sandbox detonating the sample from a corporate range (whitelist known research hosts)
  • Security appliance actively probing the C2 for enrichment
  • Shared-hosting IP reuse if the adversary infrastructure is later repurposed (validate against current IOC feeds)
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: identify the InitiatingProcess and port — svchost/frontpage.exe on 5003 or 3522 strongly confirms HelloNet; a browser hit may be incidental. 2) CONTAIN: block both IPs at the perimeter, isolate the host, and capture netflow for scoping. 3) HUNT: enumerate every internal host that contacted either IP, then pivot to UC1 (side-load), UC3 (tesh4RPC.txt), and UC6 (svchost listeners) on each.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in ("5.39.253.206", "176.32.34.135")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("5.39.253.206", "176.32.34.135")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkApplicationProtocol, DvcAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc

HelloProxy listener: svchost.exe binding TCP 5003/5060 AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the injected HelloProxy component, which after hooking AFD listens on ports 5003 and 5060 inside svchost.exe awaiting C2 commands. A svchost process creating a listening socket on these non-standard ports is highly anomalous. Rationale: Article states HelloProxy 'starts listening on ports 5003 and 5060' from within svchost after injection. svchost.exe is not a normal listener on these ports. Sentinel/Sigma/Datadog/Falcon omitted: none of the tenant-available tables cleanly express a Windows listening-socket-created event (Sysmon does not emit listeners by default; ImNetworkSession lacks listener semantics), so this is deliberately Defender-native. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/tr/hellonet-vipnet/120700/
ATT&CKT1571 T1090.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A genuine SIP/VoIP service or softphone binding 5060 (verify hosting process is not svchost -netsvcs)
  • Legitimate service hosted in svchost that a third-party product registered on 5003
  • Port-reuse by an unrelated internal application after the malicious process exits
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has @"\Windows\System32\" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "netsvcs"
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: confirm the listening svchost's command line is the -netsvcs variant and check for the sibling wtsapi32.dll side-load (UC1) and tesh4RPC.txt (UC3) on the host. 2) CONTAIN: isolate the host, capture a memory image of the svchost (HelloProxy runs in memory), then suspend/kill it and block the C2 IPs. 3) HUNT: sweep for any svchost listening on 5003/5060 fleet-wide and correlate with inbound connections to those ports and outbound to 5.39.253.206/176.32.34.135.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType == "ListeningConnectionCreated"
| where LocalPort in (5003, 5060)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "svchost.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, LocalPort, Protocol, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActionType == "ListeningConnectionCreated"
| where LocalPort in (5003, 5060)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "svchost.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, LocalPort, Protocol, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("16c211c96735f2fae9361b89bd7a31bf", "1bfe2b9493128574907a8279256a8bcc", "f9eed2f0158dc98e7012fb809152209c", "6001829a128fe264b4403138700c11a8", "ee4ff46ddd8489e81447962f927bc3f6", "41c938b3cd7e55d4077e34976929b140", "b103cd21280b4061f88b2bcc51394894", "9f5606a0755bc633b9bd7db6d179c09e", "0cfdffc56f0fa325d0c4d24780b46597") or SHA1 in~ ("16c211c96735f2fae9361b89bd7a31bf", "1bfe2b9493128574907a8279256a8bcc", "f9eed2f0158dc98e7012fb809152209c", "6001829a128fe264b4403138700c11a8", "ee4ff46ddd8489e81447962f927bc3f6", "41c938b3cd7e55d4077e34976929b140", "b103cd21280b4061f88b2bcc51394894", "9f5606a0755bc633b9bd7db6d179c09e", "0cfdffc56f0fa325d0c4d24780b46597") or MD5 in~ ("16c211c96735f2fae9361b89bd7a31bf", "1bfe2b9493128574907a8279256a8bcc", "f9eed2f0158dc98e7012fb809152209c", "6001829a128fe264b4403138700c11a8", "ee4ff46ddd8489e81447962f927bc3f6", "41c938b3cd7e55d4077e34976929b140", "b103cd21280b4061f88b2bcc51394894", "9f5606a0755bc633b9bd7db6d179c09e", "0cfdffc56f0fa325d0c4d24780b46597")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("16c211c96735f2fae9361b89bd7a31bf", "1bfe2b9493128574907a8279256a8bcc", "f9eed2f0158dc98e7012fb809152209c", "6001829a128fe264b4403138700c11a8", "ee4ff46ddd8489e81447962f927bc3f6", "41c938b3cd7e55d4077e34976929b140", "b103cd21280b4061f88b2bcc51394894", "9f5606a0755bc633b9bd7db6d179c09e", "0cfdffc56f0fa325d0c4d24780b46597") or SHA1 in~ ("16c211c96735f2fae9361b89bd7a31bf", "1bfe2b9493128574907a8279256a8bcc", "f9eed2f0158dc98e7012fb809152209c", "6001829a128fe264b4403138700c11a8", "ee4ff46ddd8489e81447962f927bc3f6", "41c938b3cd7e55d4077e34976929b140", "b103cd21280b4061f88b2bcc51394894", "9f5606a0755bc633b9bd7db6d179c09e", "0cfdffc56f0fa325d0c4d24780b46597") or MD5 in~ ("16c211c96735f2fae9361b89bd7a31bf", "1bfe2b9493128574907a8279256a8bcc", "f9eed2f0158dc98e7012fb809152209c", "6001829a128fe264b4403138700c11a8", "ee4ff46ddd8489e81447962f927bc3f6", "41c938b3cd7e55d4077e34976929b140", "b103cd21280b4061f88b2bcc51394894", "9f5606a0755bc633b9bd7db6d179c09e", "0cfdffc56f0fa325d0c4d24780b46597")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["16c211c96735f2fae9361b89bd7a31bf", "1bfe2b9493128574907a8279256a8bcc", "f9eed2f0158dc98e7012fb809152209c", "6001829a128fe264b4403138700c11a8", "ee4ff46ddd8489e81447962f927bc3f6", "41c938b3cd7e55d4077e34976929b140", "b103cd21280b4061f88b2bcc51394894", "9f5606a0755bc633b9bd7db6d179c09e", "0cfdffc56f0fa325d0c4d24780b46597"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

// Article-specific bespoke detection — HelloNet campaign: new malicious modules launched through the ViPNet update syst

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("wtsapi32.dll", "itcsrvup64.exe", "frontpage.exe", "itcsrvup.exe", "puh.exe", "store.exe", "amgmt.dll", "selfname.dll", "amgmt.bat", "insru.cmd", "7z.exe", "autoit3.exe", "pagent.exe") or FolderPath has_any ("C:\users\public\tesh4RPC.txt", "\ProgramData\Infotecs\ViPNet", "C:\Users\Public\music", "C:\users\public\music\frontpage.exe"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,

| order by Timestamp desc

Two-phase attacks with the GoSerpent backdoor, Stowaway RAT, ThumbcacheService and other tools aim to steal data from government entities in Southeast Asia.

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — GoSerpent: a persistent threat evolves with sophisticated data collection and ex
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] GoSerpent/McMx masquerading proxy binaries lass.exe and updates.exe · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] GoSerpent ThumbcacheService staging DB (thumbcache_605a.db) written to C:\Users\Public · [LLM] GoSerpent 7-Zip archiving with hardcoded campaign password @vx0a9n5W2M0c3D6.# · [LLM] GoSerpent QuarksDumpLocalHash / SAM hive local hash extraction · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
GoSerpent ThumbcacheService staging DB (thumbcache_605a.db) written to C:\Users\Public AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts creation of the ThumbcacheService collection database thumbcache_605a.db in C:\Users\Public\, where GoSerpent stages harvested .doc/.docx/.pdf/.xls/.xlsx documents before exfiltration. Legitimate Windows thumbnail caches use the same thumbcache_*.db naming but live under AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows\Explorer, never in the Public profile, making the Public-path variant article-specific. Rationale: Anchored on the article's verbatim filename thumbcache_605a.db (code block) and the C:\Users\Public\ staging path; legitimate thumbcache DBs never live in the Public profile, so the path variant catches renamed samples with near-zero FP. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/goserpent-backdoor-in-southeast-asia/120687/
ATT&CKT1074.001 T1119
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A user or admin manually copying their AppData thumbnail cache into C:\Users\Public for troubleshooting
  • Backup/migration tooling that mirrors user profile Explorer caches into a shared Public folder
  • Forensic/IR tools exporting thumbcache artifacts to C:\Users\Public for analysis
  • A security researcher detonating the sample in a lab on a monitored host
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has @"\Windows\explorer.exe"
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify InitiatingProcessFileName that wrote the DB; a service DLL host (svchost.exe hosting an unknown service) or a binary in Public/Temp is high-suspicion. Inspect the file for a 7-Zip archive nearby and confirm it is not a genuine Explorer cache. 2) Contain: isolate the host, capture the DB and any adjacent .7z archives for analysis, and disable/stop the suspicious Windows service backing ThumbcacheService. 3) Hunt: pivot on the same host for 7-Zip archiving with the campaign password, lass.exe/updates.exe processes, and SAM/LSASS credential-dumping activity in the prior days.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "thumbcache_605a.db"
    or (FolderPath has @"\Users\Public\" and FileName startswith "thumbcache_" and FileName endswith ".db")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "thumbcache_605a.db"
    or (TargetFilePath has @"\Users\Public\" and TargetFileName startswith "thumbcache_" and TargetFileName endswith ".db")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

GoSerpent 7-Zip archiving with hardcoded campaign password @vx0a9n5W2M0c3D6.# AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts ThumbcacheService's 7-Zip archiving stage, which packs collected documents into password-protected archives using the fixed password @vx0a9n5W2M0c3D6.# with a 20MB volume limit. The password string is a unique campaign artifact, so any command line containing it is effectively a signature regardless of the archiver binary name. Rationale: The password @vx0a9n5W2M0c3D6.# is a verbatim campaign string with effectively zero legitimate use; matching its alphanumeric core (vx0a9n5W2M0c3D6) survives quoting/escaping and catches renamed 7z binaries. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/goserpent-backdoor-in-southeast-asia/120687/
ATT&CKT1560.001 T1074.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Analyst re-running the sample's archive command during malware analysis on a lab host
  • Threat-intel/IR playbook that references the password string in a script comment for testing detections
  • Purple-team exercise emulating GoSerpent's archiving stage
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the archiver binary (7z.exe/7za.exe or a renamed copy) and the target file set; look for the -v20m volume flag and the source documents being packed. 2) Contain: isolate the host, preserve the produced archives, and block outbound to any network share the archives were destined for. 3) Hunt: locate thumbcache_605a.db on the same host, review the credential-dumping activity that supplied the share credentials, and check network-share write events for exfiltration of the archives.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "vx0a9n5W2M0c3D6"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where CommandLine has "vx0a9n5W2M0c3D6"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

GoSerpent/McMx masquerading proxy binaries lass.exe and updates.exe AIInstallation High
Hunts execution of GoSerpent's masquerading binaries lass.exe (mimicking lsass.exe) and updates.exe, which host the SOCKS5 proxy/RAT. lass.exe is never a legitimate Windows binary, and updates.exe running from user-writable/staging directories is a strong anomaly for this campaign. Rationale: lass.exe and updates.exe are named verbatim in the article (code blocks) as GoSerpent's process-masquerading filenames; lass.exe has no legitimate counterpart and the path constraint on updates.exe filters the common legitimate updater binaries. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/goserpent-backdoor-in-southeast-asia/120687/
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1090.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate third-party application shipping its own updates.exe from ProgramData/AppData (e.g. some auto-updaters)
  • Developer/test binary coincidentally named lass.exe in a source tree
  • Software packaging or installer temp extraction dropping an updates.exe into a Temp directory
  • Portable app launched from a USB/Public share named updates.exe
Suppression filter
| where not (FileName =~ "updates.exe" and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("msiexec.exe","setup.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the SHA256 and signer of the process; unsigned lass.exe or a Go-compiled updates.exe from a user-writable path is high-confidence. Check for a listening socket / SOCKS5 behavior and outbound C2 from the same PID. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the process, and block the associated C2 IPs at the perimeter. 3) Hunt: search for ThumbcacheService staging (thumbcache_605a.db), the 7-Zip archive password, and credential-dumping tools deployed by the same backdoor across the environment.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName =~ "lass.exe"
    or (FileName =~ "updates.exe" and FolderPath has_any (@"\Users\Public\", @"\Temp\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\AppData\"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetProcessName endswith @"\lass.exe" or TargetProcessName =~ "lass.exe"
    or ((TargetProcessName endswith @"\updates.exe" or TargetProcessName =~ "updates.exe") and TargetProcessName has_any (@"\Users\Public\", @"\Temp\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\AppData\"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

GoSerpent QuarksDumpLocalHash / SAM hive local hash extraction AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the QuarksDumpLocalHash tool GoSerpent deploys to extract local account password hashes from the SAM registry hive for offline cracking, plus the equivalent reg.exe SAM/SECURITY hive save. This is distinct from LSASS memory access and targets the on-disk SAM credential store. Rationale: Anchored on the named tool QuarksDumpLocalHash and its documented SAM-hive extraction behavior; the reg.exe hive-save branch catches the same TTP if the operator uses a LOLBin instead of the custom tool, and it deliberately avoids overlapping the existing LSASS-access detection. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/goserpent-backdoor-in-southeast-asia/120687/
ATT&CKT1003.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sysadmin exporting a SAM/SECURITY hive for legitimate password-audit or migration tooling
  • Endpoint hardening/audit software (e.g. compliance scanners) reading local hive backups
  • IR/forensics collection scripts that reg save HKLM\SAM for evidence
  • Backup software snapshotting registry hives
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("forensic_collector.exe","psexec.exe") and not (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "cmd.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "backup")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the parent process and account; a hive save or quarks* binary spawned by an unknown Go backdoor (lass.exe/updates.exe) rather than an admin session is high-confidence. Check whether the resulting hive/hash output was written to a staging path. 2) Contain: isolate the host, force-reset local account passwords (and any domain accounts used interactively), and revoke cached credentials. 3) Hunt: correlate with ThumbcacheService staging and network-share writes — the dumped credentials are used to authenticate to shares for exfiltration; review share-access logs for the affected accounts.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName has "quarks" or ProcessCommandLine has "QuarksDumpLocalHash"
    or (FileName =~ "reg.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "save" and ProcessCommandLine has_any (@"hklm\sam", @"hklm\security"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has "quarks" or CommandLine has "QuarksDumpLocalHash"
    or (NewProcessName endswith @"\reg.exe" and CommandLine has "save" and (CommandLine has @"hklm\sam" or CommandLine has @"hklm\security"))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/quarks/i OR CommandLine=/QuarksDumpLocalHash/i OR (ImageFileName=/\\reg\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/save/i AND CommandLine=/hklm\\(sam|security)/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="*quarks*" OR Processes.process="*QuarksDumpLocalHash*" OR (Processes.process_name="reg.exe" AND Processes.process="*save*" AND (Processes.process="*hklm\\sam*" OR Processes.process="*hklm\\security*"))) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="*quarks*" OR Processes.process="*QuarksDumpLocalHash*" OR (Processes.process_name="reg.exe" AND Processes.process="*save*" AND (Processes.process="*hklm\\sam*" OR Processes.process="*hklm\\security*"))) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:

      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT

      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
